prose_updates.tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. The main result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this entire nonlinear path. An observed plug-in welfare frontier supplies the operational temperature selector, while a deterministic simultaneous-event bridge transfers coverage to the oracle regret at that selected temperature. An effective interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm emits a machine-checkable one-sided certificate within an explicit work bound and has a finite analytic fallback. The resulting envelope remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. A cellwise atom formula and a legal two-stratum binary collision witness show that the frozen assumptions do not imply a uniform atom-removed small-interval modulus, so two-sided critical-value accuracy requires additional structure even though one-sided honesty does not.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while the hard assignment boundary and softmax inference for one predetermined smoothing sequence are studied separately. No published result gives a quantitative joint law or a certified one-sided critical value over the full penalty menu, and Gaussian-supremum anti-concentration does not cover collisions of the hard-cell atoms exhibited here.
project_justification.niche: Finite multiaction lotteries create a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic: its interior coordinates are nonlinear Gaussian transforms, its hard endpoint is directionally differentiable with benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and its opposite endpoint has a different quadratic normalization. Its hard cells also generate explicitly characterizable atoms whose levels can collide as the local state varies.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a verified lower CDF bracket with directed rounding and a finite fallback into computably honest inference after frontier-based temperature choice. It also proves the exact hard-cell atom formula and a fixed legal counterexample to uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, sharply separating the settled one-sided guarantee from unavailable two-sided value accuracy.

prose_updates.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie studies benchmark-centered KL assignment and proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty; its Conclusion leaves data-driven penalty choice open, and its deterministic binary analysis is separate. Its three-arm commitment-savings frontier motivates an illustration, but no finite-stratification adequacy claim is made. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis uses softmax smoothing for one unsmoothed optimal-policy value along a predetermined diverging temperature, a different scalar target. Hirano--Porter supplies the shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment for binary hard treatment choice, not a multiaction path law. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato and Giessing give anti-concentration for Gaussian-process suprema, whereas \(G(h,Z_V)\) is nonlinear and the proved hard-cell atom collisions rule out the requested uniform atom-removed modulus under the present class. Fang--Santos explains directional irregularity but does not furnish atom-safe continuum calibration. Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki provide Gaussian integration components, not certification of this nonlinear continuum event. Kang supplies simultaneous-band selection logic for an observed series path; the present bridge additionally separates the observed selector frontier from the unobserved oracle causal-regret target.
prose_updates.interpretation: The robust output is deliberately one-sided: it certifies that the entire normalized oracle-regret path lies below one auditable critical value, so any temperature chosen from observed data inherits the same guarantee. The negative concentration theorem is not a failure of coverage. It says that nearby local states can place positive hard-cell atoms arbitrarily close together, preventing a uniform conversion from probability error to critical-value error without further separation or atom-structure assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The one-sided algorithm terminates and certifies coverage because work-capped refinement has an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback. It need not return a critical value within a prescribed numerical distance of \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\). The proved two-stratum binary witness shows that no uniform atom-removed modulus follows from the frozen assumptions: distinct positive hard-cell atoms can collide while retaining positive mass. Thus a two-sided value-width certificate would need additional atom separation, a restricted local-state set, or another explicit structural condition. The rational fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) can be conservative.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem is uniform only for fixed \(J\) and \(K\), positive benchmark probabilities, positive stratum and treatment probabilities, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, and a covariance spectrum bounded away from zero. It excludes boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing action or stratum counts, disappearing cells, and continuous covariates without a prespecified finite stratification. The commitment-savings display is an illustration conditional on prespecified cells. Temperature selection is restricted to \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable rules, including rules based on the displayed plug-in frontier; that frontier is not claimed to estimate the unobserved oracle regret path. The simultaneous upper envelope and its exact transfer to operational selectors are settled. The requested uniform atom-removed anti-concentration statement is false in general on the declared model, and no two-sided least-favorable quantile-accuracy guarantee is claimed without added separation structure.

statement_notes.justification: A one-sided critical value remains operationally honest when every real input has an effective name, every rounding direction is independently checkable, and a verified analytic fallback guarantees termination even at atoms.
statement_notes.gap: Existing Gaussian integration engines address supplied rectangles or orthants; they do not certify this nonlinear continuum sublevel event or its least-favorable parameter envelope.
statement_notes.consumer: The algorithm turns the path approximation into an auditable conservative critical value for low-dimensional multiaction experiments.

statement_notes.justification: This is the operational selection-valid coverage theorem: the temperature is chosen from observed data, the covered quantity is oracle causal regret, and the one-sided ramp remains correct at every quantile atom.
statement_notes.gap: Gaussian anti-concentration and regular quantile inversion do not handle the nonlinear hard-cell atom collisions proved in this note; the theorem instead uses a verified lower CDF bracket.
statement_notes.consumer: A planner may inspect the sample-computable frontier, choose a temperature measurably, and report a certified upper bound for oracle regret at that chosen point.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem identifies every hard-cell atom and proves by a fixed legal binary design that removing the atom at the left endpoint does not restore uniform small-interval control.
statement_notes.gap: Gaussian-process anti-concentration does not apply to this nonlinear supremum, and the explicit collision witness shows that the desired modulus is false under the declared class rather than merely unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: Implementers know that the one-sided certificate is sound, while a two-sided critical-value tolerance requires an additional separation or atom-structure condition.
